sidebar.emptyBody: Bots you create appear here. Make one and tell it the job: it writes its own instructions from your answer.

landing.note: A new bot gets a name and asks for its job. Tell it, and it sets itself up; change anything later in its settings.

chat.hello: Ask {{name}} anything. It can read your sessions and act on them.

placeholders.session: Ask {{name}} to check on a session…

chat.tooLong: This message is {{length}} characters long; a bot takes up to {{max}}.
chat.noKey: {{provider}} has no key in this workspace yet. Add one to talk to this bot.
chat.failedUnknown: The turn ended without saying why.

failure.rate_limit: {{provider}} is limiting requests for now. This usually passes: try again in a moment.
failure.usage_limit: The {{provider}} account is out of quota or credit. Sending it again won't help until it is topped up or the plan resets.
failure.credential: {{provider}} refused the key or sign-in. Sending it again won't help: check it in Model providers.
failure.refused: {{provider}} refused this request. Sending it again won't help: change the message or the model.
failure.unavailable: {{provider}} could not be reached. This is usually temporary: try again in a moment.
failure.context: This turn filled {{provider}}'s context faster than it could be compacted, so it stopped: {{provider}} refused nothing. Sending it again won't help: ask it to read less at once (a smaller file, a shorter output), or split the request.
failure.time_limit: This turn ran out of time. Sending it again won't help: ask for a smaller step, or split the request.
failure.step_limit: This turn used all its steps and stopped before it finished. Sending it again won't help: ask for a smaller step, or say go on to continue.
failure.stalled: {{provider}} sent nothing for 5 minutes, so this turn stopped. This is usually temporary: try again in a moment.
failure.loop: This turn kept repeating calls that changed nothing, so it stopped. Sending it again won't help: say what to do differently.
failure.interrupted: This turn was interrupted before it finished. Sending it again runs it.
failure.storage: We could not save this turn, so it stopped: the fault is ours, not {{provider}}'s. Try again in a moment.

chat.olderFailed: Earlier messages could not be loaded. Scroll up again to try once more.

images.notSupported: {{name}} isn't an image a bot can read. Use a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP.
images.tooMany: A message can carry up to {{max}} images.
images.noVision: {{model}} can't read images. Switch the bot's model to send them.
images.noVisionHeld: {{model}} can't read images. Remove them or switch the model to send this message.
images.uploading: Wait for the images to finish adding.
images.failedHeld: Remove the image that couldn't be added.

skills.title: Skills

builtIn.hint: Oppenheimer gives these to every bot. You can read them, but not change or delete them.

dialog.description: A skill is a recipe the bot follows: when it applies, the steps, how to check the result and what to report.
dialog.name: Name

dialog.summaryHint: One sentence on what it does and when to use it. The bot reads this in every chat.

1. List the pull requests merged since the last tag.
2. Group them by area.

routines.subtitle: Work the bot does on a schedule or when something happens.
routines.empty: Routines are tasks this bot runs on a schedule or when something happens. Ask it in chat to set one up.

dialog.title: Edit “{{name}}”
dialog.description: Change what the routine is called and what it asks the bot on every run.
dialog.name: Name
dialog.promptHint: What the bot does on every run, as you would ask it in chat.
dialog.whenHint: To change when it runs, ask the bot in chat.

routines.deleteBody: This deletes the routine and stops its future runs. This can't be undone.
routines.loadFailed: Could not load the bot's routines.

webhookUrl.revokeBody: Anything posted to it is refused from now on. The routine keeps its webhook trigger: create a new URL to use it again.
webhookUrl.dialogBody: Anything that can send a POST (a deploy pipeline, Sentry, a form) runs this routine through this URL. The bot reads what was posted as outside data, never as instructions.
webhookUrl.replaces: The URL it has now stops working as soon as the new one is made.
webhookUrl.signed: Require a signature (a signing secret every request is signed with)
webhookUrl.shownOnce: Copy them now: they’re shown once. Afterwards only the start of the URL is shown.
webhookUrl.signHow: Send x-oppenheimer-signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of “<t>.<body>” with this secret>. Requests more than five minutes old are refused.

homeHost.title: Home host
homeHost.subtitle: Your bot always runs in Oppenheimer. When it starts a coding session and you haven't named a machine, the session runs here.
homeHost.noneHint: The bot asks which machine to use each time it starts a session.
homeHost.noHostsBody: A bot starts its coding sessions on a machine you own. Add one, then pick it here.
homeHost.failed: Could not change the home host.

permissions.title: Permissions
permissions.subtitle: What the bot does on its own, and what it asks you first.
permissions.loadFailed: Could not load the bot’s permissions.

preset.ask: Tools you leave on their default follow Ask for approval: anything that reaches outside Oppenheimer asks first.
preset.auto: Tools you leave on their default follow Approve for me: anything that reaches outside Oppenheimer goes to a reviewer first, which lets what you asked for run and leaves the rest to you. A tool you set to Ask always asks.
preset.full: Tools you leave on their default follow Full access: they run without asking, the ones that always ask included. Sending mail, and what you set to Ask or a rule asks for, still wait for your yes.

permissions.perCall: Every call asks: it is never allowed for good.
permissions.noGrants: Nothing yet. “Always allow for …” on a request adds it here.

ask.title: Ask me first when
ask.hint: A matching request waits for you, even where the tool would run on its own.
ask.placeholder: e.g. it mentions payments or customer data

allow.title: Go ahead without asking when
allow.hint: A matching request runs without a card. An ask rule that also matches wins.
allow.placeholder: e.g. it comments on our docs repository

gateways.isDefault: The default bot on this number
gateways.noDefault: No default bot on this number
gateways.noneHere: This bot answers no chat by name on this number yet.
gateways.routeFailed: That did not save. Try again.
gateways.addDescription: Pick the groups and people this bot answers on this number. A chat another bot answers moves to this one.
gateways.telegramMeta: Answers you there. Groups and other people on Telegram come next.
gateways.noTelegram: No Telegram bot answers as this bot yet. Pick it for one in Settings → Telegram.

slack.title: Slack
slack.subtitle: Give this bot its own Slack app, so you can ask it with a mention in a channel or in its direct messages. It answers in the thread you asked in.
slack.loadFailed: Couldn't load this bot's Slack app.
slack.howItWorks: The bot answers only you: anyone else who mentions it is ignored. Approvals stay in Oppenheimer and your Inbox; the thread gets a link to them. Write stop in a thread to stop what it's doing there.
slack.stepCreateHint: Slack opens with the bot's name, the permissions it needs and where to send its events already filled in. Pick your workspace and create it.
slack.stepInstallHint: In the app's settings, open Install App and choose Install to Workspace.
slack.stepPaste: Paste its token and signing secret
slack.stepPasteHint: Both are kept encrypted and never shown again.
slack.tokenHint: Under OAuth & Permissions, once the app is installed. It starts with xoxb-.
slack.replaceDescription: Paste the token and signing secret again, after reinstalling the app or rotating its token. A different app will need you to link your Slack user again.
slack.disconnectDescription: Oppenheimer forgets the app's token and the bot stops answering in Slack. Its threads stay in the bot's history. The app stays in Slack; delete it there to remove it.
slack.ownerIntro: @{{name}} answers only you. Tell it which Slack user is you by sending it a one-time code.
slack.ownerStepSend: Send it this message within ten minutes

delete.title: Delete “{{name}}”?
delete.description: The bot, its instructions, its memory and its conversation are removed for good.
